Article Title: Deepam row: Members of Hindu outfits protest, clash with cops as lamp not lit at 'Deepathoon'
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A scuffle broke out between members of Hindu outfits and Tamil Nadu Police on Tuesday at Thiruparankundram after the Karthigai Deepam was lit at the usual spot instead of the ‘Deepathoon’, despite the Supreme Court 's order.Leaders of Hindu outfits and BJP staged a protest at the entrance to the hill pathway and raised slogans against the government.Officials tried to disperse the protesters and warned them of a lathi charge if they continued their demonstration.“The gathering you have assembled is an unlawful assembly. Disperse immediately, otherwise you will have to be dispersed by lathi charge,” read a placard displayed by the police.This comes after the ceremonial lamp was lit atop the Arulmigu Uchipillayar Temple in Thiruparankundram, instead of at the disputed stone pillar, or ‘Deepathoon’, atop Thiruparankundram hill, as directed by the Supreme Court.The ceremony was held amid heightened security, with police detaining several people citing apprehensions of disorder based on intelligence inputs and their past conduct.Several BJP leaders and members of Hindu organisations were also detained across Tamil Nadu as police enforced restrictions ahead of the ceremony.Later in the day, the Madras high court's Madurai Bench, however, directed the Tamil Nadu government and all authorities concerned to comply with the Supreme Court's November 20 order permitting the ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon.It also directed officials to release all persons unlawfully detained under prohibitory orders imposed in Thiruparankundram.The direction was issued to the district collector, police commissioner and temple authorities amid restrictions surrounding the ceremony.The dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thiruparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.The Subramaniya Swamy Temple is situated at the foothills, while a Dargah is located near the hilltop. A Shiva temple is also situated on the hill.Hindu groups maintain that the stone pillar where they seek to light the lamp belongs to the temple, citing civil court decisions dating back about a century.Dargah officials and Muslim organisations have opposed the proposed lighting, citing its proximity to their place of worship. The dispute involves questions of ownership and the rights of the respective parties.On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah.The apex court specified that the ceremony must be conducted by an authorised team and barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.
Article Summary: The Karthigai Deepam was lit at the usual spot instead of the ‘Deepathoon’, despite the Supreme Court's order. This comes after the ceremonial lamp was lit atop the Arulmigu Uchipillayar Temple in Thiruparankundram, instead of at the disputed stone pillar.

Article Title: 'Distorted portrayal': Sonia Gandhi gets legal notice over VD Savarkar's remarks in memoir
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar's grandnephew has sent a legal notice to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi , demanding an unconditional apology and correction over remarks about the freedom fighter in her memoir, alleging a "distorted portrayal" of his ancestor.Satyaki Savarkar, the paternal grandnephew of VD Savarkar, has objected to statements on pages 201 and 443 of the book,alleging that they are factually inaccurate, historically misleading and prejudicial to Savarkar's reputation and legacy, PTI reported.The notice, issued by advocate Sangram Kolhatkar on Satyaki Savarkar's behalf, asks Sonia Gandhi to meet the demands within 15 days of receiving it.It warns that failure to comply could prompt legal proceedings before a competent court or authority.The notice refers to a statement on page 201 of the memoir, which reads, "While Congress freedom fighters were enduring assaults and imprisonment at the hands of the British rulers, senior ideologues of the RSS like Vinayak Damodar Savarkar were writing mercy petitions to their colonial masters, and their members were colluding with the British authorities as informers."Satyaki Savarkar alleges that the statement creates an impression that VD Savarkar was involved in informing on or collaborating with the British authorities against Indian freedom fighters.The notice disputes this implication, saying it is unsupported by the historical context of Savarkar's imprisonment, petitions and political activities.It states that Savarkar endured prolonged imprisonment and severe hardships under British rule, including incarceration in the Cellular Jail in the Andaman Islands.It further argues that references to his petitions without examining the circumstances and historical background present an incomplete and distorted account of his life and political struggle.The notice also objects to a statement on page 443, which reads, "A contrary vision, articulated by Gandhiji's contemporary Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, the founder of the ideology known as Hindutva, views India as primarily a nation where Hindus are supreme-an outlook espoused by the RSS, the BJP, and their numerous affiliates across the country known collectively as the 'Sangh Parivar,' or 'Family of the RSS'."It alleges that the passage oversimplifies and misrepresents Savarkar's political and ideological philosophy, arguing that his writings, speeches and views need to be considered in their proper historical, intellectual and political context.According to the notice, the two statements, when read together, present a distorted account of Savarkar's role in the freedom struggle and his political philosophy, potentially misleading readers and creating an unjustified adverse impression of his legacy.The legal notice also refers to actions taken by the government during former prime minister Indira Gandhi's tenure and her personal contributions, which it says recognised Savarkar's stature as a patriot and freedom fighter.It cites the issuance of a commemorative postage stamp in Savarkar's honour, as well as Indira Gandhi's personal contribution of Rs 11,000 from her bank account towards the Swatantryaveer Savarkar Rashtriya Smarak.It argues that these official acts and Indira Gandhi's personal contribution demonstrate recognition of Savarkar's patriotism and asks Sonia Gandhi to explain how the statements in her memoir can be reconciled with these records.The notice calls on Sonia Gandhi to substantiate the statements with authentic historical material or acknowledge "inaccuracies and misleading implications" and take corrective measures.It seeks a written, unequivocal and unconditional apology for the statements, along with a public clarification explaining their historical basis, context and intended meaning and acknowledging and correcting any factual inaccuracies or misleading implications.It also asks Sonia Gandhi to take appropriate steps, in consultation with HarperCollins Publishers India, to "correct, suitably qualify or withdraw the objectionable statements from subsequent editions, reprints and electronic versions of the publication".The notice states that the memoir, authored by Sonia Gandhi and published by HarperCollins Publishers India, was reportedly released on November 10.Satyaki Savarkar said he recently came across the book and was disturbed by the statements and imputations concerning VD Savarkar.
Article Summary: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar's grandnephew has sent a legal notice to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi. He is demanding an unconditional apology and correction over remarks about the freedom fighter in her memoir. The notice alleges a "distorted portrayal" of his ancestor.

Article Title: 6 samples collected, 5 met applicable standards: Bisleri
Article Text:
The company said it follows a 10-stage purification process, conducts over 90 quality tests and will cooperate with FSSAI.

NEW DELHI: Chemical contaminants detected in a batch of packaged drinking water manufactured by Bisleri at its Goa facility has raised concerns over potential health risks, including kidney damage and cancer.Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) reportedly declared the sample unsafe after tests flagged bromate and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Bisleri, however, has disputed the findings, maintaining that its water is safe for consumption.Dr Tanmay Pandya, HoD and director, Nephrology and Renal Transplantation, Sarvodaya Hospital, Faridabad, said prolonged exposure to certain chemical contaminants could affect kidney function, depending on their concentration and duration of exposure. "Bromate is a chemical of concern because of its potential carcinogenic properties," he said, adding that certain heavy metals and industrial chemicals could also interfere with kidney function.In a statement issued Monday, Bisleri said FSSAI collected six samples from its Goa manufacturing facility on Sept 30, 2025.While five met the applicable standards, the sixth recorded bromate at 12 micrograms per litre against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre, the company said in a statement.Following an appeal, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory in Nov 2025. Bisleri said the laboratory found bromate within the prescribed limit but separately flagged PAHs. The company subsequently got the sample tested at an FSSAI-approved independent laboratory, which also found bromate within the prescribed limit.Bisleri said it submitted the independent laboratory results to FSSAI's Western Regional Office on Feb 2, 2026, but received no further communication. It also claimed it had not received the reported notice by email or in hard copy.The company said it follows a 10-stage purification process, conducts over 90 quality tests and will cooperate with FSSAI.Explaining the contamination concerns, Dr Saurabh Arora, MD of Auriga Research, said packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are regulated under separate standards. Bromate can form during water treatment, while PAHs may enter through packaging or contamination during bottling.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) reportedly declared the sample unsafe. Tests flagged bromate and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) Bisleri has disputed the findings, maintaining that its water is safe for consumption.

Article Title: Bangladeshi court orders interim curbs on social media access for children under 16
Article Text:
The court issued the directives Sunday while passing an order on a writ petition

DHAKA: Bangladeshi court has directed the authorities to frame mandatory interim guidelines to prevent children below 16 years of age from accessing social media platforms and ordered the formation of an independent expert committee to examine the impact of algorithm-driven content feeds on minors.The High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh issued the directives on Sunday while passing an order on a writ petition that questioned the government's failure to formulate a national policy regulating social media access for children under 16, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.The bench comprising Justices Sikder Mahmudur Razi and Fatema Anwar directed the Secretary of the Posts and Telecommunications Division and the Chairman of the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission, among other respondents, to take necessary steps.It also ordered the immediate formation of a committee comprising cybersecurity specialists, child psychologists, paediatricians and legal experts to assess the structural impact of algorithm-controlled feeds on children.The move comes amid growing international concerns over the impact of social media on children's mental health, physical well-being and development, with governments across the globe increasingly considering age-based restrictions and stricter safeguards against potentially harmful online content.The committee will examine how algorithm-based recommendation systems influence children's behaviour, exposure to online content and overall development, and submit its assessment to help shape regulatory measures.The writ petition was filed earlier this month by Supreme Court lawyer Mohammad Faisal Dastagir, who appeared before the court in person.The absence of a regulatory framework had left children below 16 exposed to unrestricted social media use, potentially affecting their mental and physical development, Dastagir was quoted as saying by Prothom Alo.Citing research highlighting health concerns, including impaired eyesight, among children exposed to excessive screen time, he argued that a national policy was necessary to regulate their access to social media.The court also directed the authorities to explain why their failure to establish an independent committee to assess the structural impact of algorithm-controlled feeds on minors and formulate a national policy restricting social media access for children under 16 should not be declared illegal and beyond their lawful authority, the report said.Several countries across the world are tightening regulations governing children's access to social media.Australia became the first country to enforce a minimum age of 16 for accounts on major social media platforms in December 2025, requiring platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent under-16s from creating or retaining accounts.Indonesia banned children under 16 from having accounts on "high-risk" social media and online platforms starting on March 28, 2026, making it the first country in Southeast Asia to introduce such restrictions.Malaysia, too, began enforcing age-verification requirements in June 2026, barring children below 16 from opening social media accounts and requiring existing users to verify their age.The UK plans to ban children under 16 from major social media platforms starting in spring 2027, with initial regulations expected to be laid before Parliament by December 2026. It is also considering overnight curfews for teens aged 16 and 17 and blocking infinite-scroll mechanisms for kids.Canada introduced a bill in parliament in June, proposing a minimum age of 16 for holding social media accounts. The proposed legislation is yet to become law.Brazil enacted rules in 2026 requiring age verification and parental account linking for users under 16.The European Commission has proposed the EU KIDS Act in September to ban children under 13 from social media and set 15 as the minimum age for independent accounts.Countries such as France, Greece, Turkey, Spain, Poland, New Zealand, Denmark, and Slovenia have drafted restrictions aimed primarily at under-15s, while Austria has proposed an under-14 ban.
Article Summary: The High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh issued the directives on Sunday. The move comes amid growing international concerns over the impact of social media on children's mental health, physical well-being and development. Several countries across the world are tightening regulations governing children's access to social media.

Article Title: China’s mega dam takes shape near Arunachal Pradesh: Satellite data
Article Text:
India has proposed 11,200MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project to cushion the impactof sudden changes in water discharge from China

GUWAHATI: Fresh satellite imagery analysis by an Indian geospatial AI deep tech start-up incubated at FITT, IIT Delhi, shows construction of China’s 60 GW Medog hydropower project on Yarlung Tsangpo (the Siang in India) is advanced and widespread.According to the findings of the public-release assessment by EarthSense Labs, entire villages had been cleared at the main dam site, river diversion works were visible and heavy industrial infrastructure had been built near the Arunachal Pradesh border.The findings are significant for India as it has proposed the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh. Project proponents say SUMP is intended to cushion the downstream impact of the Chinese project.The Chinese project is close to the McMahon Line , about 40 km to 50 km north of Arunachal Pradesh.The EarthSense report places the tunnel exit near the border, downstream of Medog County. The SUMP, proposed on Siang river, would be located further downstream in India, across Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts. Its proposed reservoir is expected by project proponents to hold nine billion cubic metres of water.The Chinese project will be a multi-structure dam system along the lower Yarlung Tsangpo river in southeastern Tibet.It will include a tunnel across the river’s famous “Great U-Bend”, multiple power stations and outlets before the river enters India, the report said.The report lists four critical locations and assets — a large dam near Mainling town, where “work has started extensively after July 2025”; a lower dam, possibly near Pai town; a tunnel through Namcha Barwa Mountain; and a tunnel outlet near the India-China border, downstream of Medog County, where work has also started.“Developmental work on the tunnel outlet area has started even before the ground-breaking ceremony,” the report said.The project is planned as five cascade stations at an estimated cost of 1.2 trillion yuan (roughly $168 billion). It would use tunnels of around 40 km to exploit a river drop of more than 2,000 metres over a stretch of about 50 km, the report said.EarthSense Labs’ study of imagery from July 2025 showed villages and farm fields at the site of the proposed Mainling high dam. By Dec 2025, the villages were cleared, the fields removed and earthwork had begun, it said.Imagery of Aug 2026 showed diversion works, the relocation of entire villages and the emergence of new roads, makeshift housing and office buildings on the north bank.The key finding, according to the report, was “Site clearance and earthwork after July 2025, followed by river diversion works by Aug 2026.”Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu has pointed out that the proposed SUMP reservoir, with a storage capacity of about 9.2 billion cubic metres (BCM), is expected to give India greater control over downstream flows. Khandu had said the Siang reservoir, with a capacity greater than the reported 5.2 BCM of China’s project, would help regulate river flows, respond to sudden changes in upstream discharge and maintain water availability during lean seasons. Khandu has repeatedly flagged the absence of a binding water-sharing treaty and transparent data-sharing arrangement with China as a major vulnerability.Opposition to SUMP has hardened on the ground. Adi communities have petitioned Union home minister Amit Shah , citing concerns over displacement, land and livelihoods. Central armed police forces were deployed near the proposed site as tensions rose over a pre-feasibility survey. In Oct, violence broke out during protests.The report documents the scale and pace of construction but does not quantify environmental damage, downstream flow effects or risks to Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. Its locations are described as indicative, and the analysis relies on satellite imagery.A video featuring Adi environmental engineer Katon Moyong criticising the proposed 11,200MW Siang dam disappeared from public view in India after Meta restricted access following a govt notice, according to a notification displayed on the Facebook post of a digital news outlet in the state that had uploaded the clip.The video, posted by Arunachal Today on Nov 21, showed Moyong — aka Abor Man — explaining his opposition to the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project during home minister Amit Shah’s visit to the state. The post now displays the message: “Video not available in India.”In a notification dated Nov 22, Meta said it had restricted the content “pursuant to a notice from Govt of India under Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, 2000”. The notice warned that sharing similar content could lead to further restrictions on the outlet’s account in India.Arunachal Today said the notification did not disclose the specific grounds or details of the govt notice. It also raised questions over the curbs on social media content concerning the contentious Siang dam debate.
Article Summary: Satellite imagery analysis by an Indian geospatial AI deep tech start-up incubated at FITT, IIT Delhi, shows construction of China’s 60 GW Medog hydropower project on Yarlung Tsangpo (the Siang in India) is advanced and widespread. The findings are significant for India as it has proposed the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh. Project proponents say SUMP is intended to cushion the downstream impact of the Chinese project.

Article Title: PM Modi is Asia's second-most effective leader after Xi, says Lowy Institute's power index
Article Text:
According to the index, ‘diplomatic influence’ was India’s strongest measure

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi climbed three places to rank as Asia's second-most effective leader, behind Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to the 2026 Asia Power Index released by Lowy Institute.According to the index, 'diplomatic influence' was India's strongest measure and held steady in a year when most countries faltered. One of the notable findings of the latest index was the improvement in the assessment of Modi's regional leadership.The Lowy Institute's expert survey rated Modi more highly for his effectiveness in advancing India's diplomatic interests in Asia. The assessment comes despite a relatively subdued Indian diplomatic profile during the Gulf conflict, which the report said weighed on perceptions of his global leadership and strategic ambition.The 2026 findings point to a more prominent Indian role in an increasingly competitive Asian strategic landscape, even as the US and China continue to dominate the regional power structure.India's gains have been driven by a combination of diplomatic engagement, regional security cooperation, investment attractiveness, cultural influence and demographic prospects. Its ability to maintain economic relationships even as regional conditions weakened also helped support its overall position.India's membership in diplomatic forums was up two places to joint second. India was represented in 17 of the summits, diplomatic clubs and regional inter-governmental organisations Lowy tracks, level with Indonesia and Thailand and only one behind China.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi climbed three places to rank as Asia's second-most effective leader, behind Chinese President Xi Jinping. According to the index, ‘diplomatic influence’ was India’s strongest measure and held steady in a year when most countries faltered. The assessment comes despite a relatively subdued Indian diplomatic profile during the Gulf conflict.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday said priority must be given to the appeals of 22 lakh people, of the total 38 lakh, seeking restoration of their names in the West Bengal electoral roll, and sought the state govt's response to allegations that voters deleted during SIR are being denied ration and benefits under various social welfare schemes.The court also said even among the 22 lakh, cases of those from wards in Kolkata Municipal Corporation should be heard ahead of others, keeping in view the upcoming civic elections.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the Calcutta HC chief justice in consultation with Election Commission must increase the number of tribunals - currently 19 - to deal with the 38 lakh appeals, filed on deletion of 90 lakh voters declared absent, shifted, duplicate or dead, or flagged for 'logical discrepancy', related to mapping.The bench also asked Election Commission to requisition additional space for housing the tribunals at various places to facilitate easy access to appellants.SC's direction came after advocate Prashant Bhushan told SC that of the 1.4 lakh appeals decided so far by tribunals, which were appointed to adjudicate a large number of appeals filed after SIR, more than 90% have been allowed leading to restoration of their names in the electoral roll.This is a strong indicator based on a large sample size to persuade the top court to direct that those who have filed appeals against deletion of their names should be allowed to vote in the coming elections, Bhushan said.Supreme Court said this was the reason for it to ask for prioritisation of appeals for restoration of names relating to various wards in KMC.Bhushan, supported by senior advocate G Sankaranarayanan, told the apex court that even though the court had categorically clarified that deletion of names from electoral roll would not have any consequence, including with regard to citizenship, beyond the chance to vote, state govt has been denying the deleted voters ration through public distribution system (PDS) and benefits under social welfare schemes, including Annapurna Yojna.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said these are bald assertions and alleged that the petitioners have not cited a single example to substantiate their claims.However, the CJI-led bench asked state govt to file response to the allegations.In a related issue, SC postponed to Wednesday hearing on state govt's appeal challenging an interim order of a division bench of Calcutta HC restraining the state EC from announcing schedule for KMC polls, in which the number of wards were increased from 144 to 209 by an amending Act. Mehta said the high court mistakenly concluded that state govt lacked the jurisdiction to carry out the exercise of increasing the number of wards and resultant adjustment of ward boundaries.
Article Summary: Supreme Court said priority must be given to the appeals of 22 lakh people, of the total 38 lakh, seeking restoration of their names in the West Bengal electoral roll. The court also said even among the 22 lakh, cases of those from wards in Kolkata Municipal Corporation should be heard ahead of others.

Article Title: India's health bill: Who really pays?
Article Text:

What changed over the decade?

By 2023–24, government spending had overtaken direct household payments.

One country, very different health bills

What happens when you walk into a hospital?

Medicines bought separately account for over 42% of what Indian households pay directly for healthcare.

Who ultimately pays?

In October 2026, a 27-year-old woman from Mathura who had lost the ability to walk underwent two complex spinal operations in Lucknow. At a private hospital, doctors estimated, the treatment could have cost Rs 6–7 lakh. Under Ayushman Bharat, she received it free, TOI reported That same month, in Odisha's Bargarh district, a daily-wage worker was borrowing money to buy medicines for his family. His son's chemotherapy was covered under Ayushman Bharat, but as TOI reported , the family's monthly medicine requirements alone amounted to Rs 20,000.Both stories point to the same reality, albeit with different outcomes. The government is now picking up a larger share of the country's health bill, yet on the ground, massive medical costs can still push individual households into financial distress.Imagine India's entire healthcare bill as Rs 100. In 2013–14, families paid Rs 64.20 directly from their pockets, the government spent Rs 28.60, and other sources financed the remaining Rs 7.20.By 2023–24, the government's share had risen to Rs 43.50, while direct household payments accounted for Rs 42.70. Other financing arrangements, including private insurance, accounted for the remaining Rs 13.80. In absolute terms, government health expenditure rose from Rs 1.30 lakh crore in 2013–14 to Rs 4.14 lakh crore in 2023–24.Direct household payments increased much more slowly, from Rs 2.91 lakh crore to Rs 4.06 lakh crore. Government spending thus exceeded direct household payments by around Rs 8,000 crore.Government expenditure first overtook direct household payments in the National Health Accounts series in 2021–22, when pandemic-related spending pushed its share to 48%. A closer look at the latest National Health Accounts reveals what lies behind these numbers.Of the Rs 4.14 lakh crore spent by the government in 2023–24, approximately Rs 1.13 lakh crore was capital expenditure on healthcare infrastructure, equipment and other long-term investments. Excluding that, government spending on current healthcare, which is the money used to provide services and goods during the year, stood at about Rs 3.01 lakh crore. Households, meanwhile, paid Rs 4.06 lakh crore directly.For every Rs 100 spent on current healthcare services and goods, the government accounted for Rs 36, while households paid Rs 48.50 directly. Other sources financed the remaining Rs 15.50.However, government spending on current healthcare also more than tripled, from about Rs 98,000 crore in 2013–14 to Rs 3.01 lakh crore in 2023–24. The government's share of current healthcare expenditure rose from 23.2% to 36%.Nearly half the decade-long decline in the household share of total healthcare spending occurred in a single year, when it fell from 58.7% to 48.8% in 2017–18. This coincided with a change in the survey used to estimate household health expenditure and preceded the September 2018 launch of PM-JAY. How much of the decline was attributable to the change in estimation remains unclear.Government health expenditure increased by approximately 219% over the decade, without adjusting for inflation. Direct household payments grew by about 40%. For every Rs 100 the government spent on health in 2013–14, it was spending about Rs 319 a decade later. For households, Rs 100 became about Rs 140.Ayushman Bharat, launched in 2018, has been a prominent initiative in this expansion. Its hospital insurance component, the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), provides eligible families with annual health cover of up to Rs 5 lakh for specified hospital treatments. In October 2024, eligibility was extended to all senior citizens aged 70 and above, irrespective of their economic status. But India's increased public spending goes well beyond hospital insurance.Government-financed health insurance schemes, including PM-JAY and state-specific schemes, accounted for Rs 33,385 crore in 2023–24, or about 8% of government health expenditure. A much larger part of public spending supports the healthcare system itself. Government spending on primary healthcare, the first point of contact for many patients, increased from about Rs 50,000 crore in 2013–14 to Rs 1.53 lakh crore in 2023–24. It accounted for roughly half of the government's current health expenditure in 2023–24.Through the National Health Mission and Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, the government has sought to expand basic consultations, maternal and childcare services, access to essential medicines and diagnostic tests. State and local governments accounted for nearly 68% of government health expenditure in 2023–24, underscoring their role in this expansion.In 2023–24, government expenditure exceeded direct household payments in 13 of the 21 states and UTs for which the National Health Accounts provided comparable estimates. In the other eight, families still paid more directly. In Uttarakhand, the government accounted for 66% of total healthcare expenditure, whereas households paid 26.7% directly. The government's share stood at 57.9% in Odisha and 59.5% in Assam.Kerala shows the opposite pattern. For every Rs 100 spent on healthcare in the state, households contributed Rs 65.20 directly, against Rs 25 from the government. In West Bengal, the figures were Rs 63 and Rs 30. State-level government expenditure figures include spending by the Union government and local bodies, not merely the state government's own health budget. The estimates for household spending are based on survey data from 2017–18, updated for subsequent years.The 2025 National Sample Survey indicated that health insurance or healthcare financing coverage has risen from fewer than one in five Indians in 2017–18 to nearly half, largely through government-sponsored schemes.At least half of outpatient treatment episodes at public facilities involved no direct medical expenditure. Average out-of-pocket medical expenditure per hospitalisation, excluding childbirth, was Rs 6,631 at public facilities against Rs 50,508 at private hospitals. While the types of treatment may differ, private hospitals, including those empanelled under government schemes, accounted for 60.3% of hospitalisations excluding childbirth.Medicines remain a major financial burden, with households spending Rs 1.71 lakh crore on separately purchased medicines in 2023–24, accounting for roughly 42% of their direct healthcare expenditure. While PM-JAY primarily covers hospitalisation, initiatives such as government free-drug programmes and Jan Aushadhi seek to reduce everyday medical costs. The number of Jan Aushadhi outlets rose from around 80 in 2014 to around 11,000 by March 2024.Families also finance healthcare through insurance premiums. Expenditure through private health insurance, which includes employer-based group cover and individual policies, rose from 3.4% of total health expenditure in 2013–14 to 10.2% in 2023–24. When we look at where healthcare funds originate, including household insurance contributions, the picture changes. Households supplied Rs 55.70 of every Rs 100 spent on current healthcare in 2023–24, down from Rs 72.90 in 2013–14. The contribution from government budgets and grants rose from Rs 21.10 to Rs 34 over the same period.There is also a cost that the National Health Accounts cannot capture: the treatment someone needed but could not afford. A patient treated free at a government hospital and someone who forgoes treatment because it is unaffordable can both record zero direct medical expenditure. Their experiences could hardly be more different. The real measure of India's healthcare progress is whether an Indian can afford to fall ill without becoming poor.
Article Summary: Medicines bought separately account for over 42% of what Indian households pay directly for healthcare. The government is now picking up a larger share of the country's health bill, yet massive medical costs can still push individual households into financial distress. Government health expenditure increased by approximately 219% over the decade, without adjusting for inflation.

NEW DELHI: India and Nepal on Monday signed eight agreements to expand cooperation in sectors including space technology, security, healthcare, agriculture and sustainable urban development, following talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.The two leaders also virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur in Nepal, and jointly inaugurated several development projects during Balen Shah’s two-day state visit to India.At a joint press conference after the talks, Modi said the two countries had taken several important decisions to strengthen bilateral relations.“I am very pleased to welcome Balendra Shah ji to India on his first bilateral visit after becoming the Prime Minister of Nepal. A few months ago, when he addressed the United Nations as the world’s youngest Prime Minister, we got a clear glimpse of his vision. Over the past few hours of our discussions, I have sensed his clear vision and commitment towards Nepal’s future and India-Nepal relations. The historic mandate given to him by the people of Nepal this year reflects the aspirations and hopes of the country’s younger generation. India has always been a partner in the development journey of a strong and prosperous Nepal.In this spirit, today we have taken several important decisions to take our relations to new heights,” PM Modi said.The prime minister also announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepali rupees (approximately Rs 15,000 crore) to support Nepal’s reconstruction and long-term development, particularly in the wake of the devastating floods in August.“We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August. Today, we announce a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepali rupees to give fresh impetus to Nepal’s reconstruction and long-term development. Our commitment will be to help affected families get their lives back on track, create new opportunities, and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” he said.PM Modi also highlighted the shared religious and cultural ties between the two countries, referring to the launch of the train service connecting Ayodhya and Janakpur.“Lord Ram and Mata Sita are symbols of our shared civilisation and faith. In 2018, on the sacred land of Janakpur, I had said that our pilgrimage sites are incomplete without Nepal, and our Lord Ram is incomplete without Nepal. In 2024, the consecration ceremony of Ram Lalla took place in Ayodhya. This historic occasion gave renewed strength to our shared faith…With the launch of the Sarayu-Kamala Express train service today, we are giving a new dimension to this sacred bond,” he said.He said India had maintained supplies of fuel and other essential goods to Nepal despite serious challenges related to oil supplies this year, and expressed confidence in the future of bilateral ties.“We will together write a golden chapter of India-Nepal relations,” PM Modi said.The Saryu-Kamala Express will connect Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal, covering around 604 km in approximately 19 hours. The regular service will operate once a week in each direction from November 28, enabling pilgrims to travel between the two religious destinations without changing trains.The inaugural run on Monday operated as a special train (No. 04295), departing from Ayodhya Dham at 12.30 pm.The eight MoUs exchanged after the delegation-level talks cover satellite communication, policing, forensic sciences, civil service training, healthcare, traditional medicine, sustainable urban development, and livestock and fisheries development.In the space and communication sector, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Nepal’s Ministry of Information and Communication signed an MoU to establish a Satellite Communication (SATCOM) Network for the utilisation of the South Asia Satellite.Two agreements aim to strengthen cooperation in policing and forensic sciences. One provides for academic and research collaboration between the National Forensic Sciences University in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, and the Crime Investigation Department of Nepal Police. The other was signed between India’s Rashtriya Raksha University and Nepal’s National Police Academy.For capacity building in public administration, the National Centre for Good Governance, under India’s Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, signed an MoU with Nepal’s Administrative Staff College under the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration. The agreement provides for training programmes for Nepalese civil servants.In healthcare, India’s Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and Nepal’s Ministry of Health and Food Safety signed an MoU on cooperation in health and medicine. The two sides also signed a government-to-government agreement on cooperation in Ayurveda and other traditional systems of medicine.The remaining two agreements provide for technical cooperation in sustainable urban development and collaboration in livestock and fisheries development.At the joint press conference, Balen Shah described India-Nepal relations as being founded on mutual respect, trust and goodwill.“Ties between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as oceans,” he said.He expressed confidence that the agreements and initiatives announced during the visit would take bilateral relations to a new level, while stressing the need for cooperation on climate change.“I am confident that these historic milestones will elevate Nepal-India relations to new heights. The need of the hour is to build on the strong foundation of this enduring relationship and lay solid pillars for the future. Our Himalayas, the sources of clean water, sustain millions across this region. The pristine rivers flowing from the Himalayas into the Ganga remind us of our future and destiny, underscoring the need to address the challenges of climate change through collective action. Nepal and India have been bound by historical, cultural and civilisational ties since the sacred era of Lord Ram and Mata Janaki,” Balen Shah said.Balen Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for a two-day state visit, his first to India since assuming office in March 2026.On Monday, PM Modi received him at Hyderabad House for the bilateral talks. Before the meeting, Shah was accorded a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan and paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at the Raj Ghat memorial.Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in a post on X that the leaders would discuss various aspects of bilateral relations and explore new avenues to deepen cooperation.Jaiswal described the ceremonial welcome as reflecting “the special warmth and enduring friendship between India and Nepal” and Shah’s visit to Raj Ghat as “A tribute to the timeless legacy of Mahatma!”
Article Summary: India and Nepal signed eight agreements to expand cooperation in sectors including space technology, security, healthcare, agriculture and sustainable urban development. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur in Nepal.

How India-US drug network operated

NEW DELHI: A man deported from the US in a drug-related case, an MBA graduate with pharmacy business links and a BTech degree-holder are among the six Indians arrested in a joint India-US investigation into a cross-border drug trafficking network, news agency PTI reported.The probe, conducted by the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and the US drug enforcement administration (DEA), has been expanded to examine the accused's alleged links and illegal dealings.The six were arrested following multi-city raids conducted between November 4 and 13. Investigators are questioning them about their connections in India and abroad, PTI reported citing officials.One of the accused, T Manoj, 27, from Telangana, was deported from the US in January 2024 for allegedly trading regulated drugs. He holds a BTech degree in Computer Science and was pursuing a master's degree in the US. Investigators are examining his links in both countries.Another accused, TD Jaiswal, 30, from Lucknow, holds an MBA degree and has business links with a pharmacy and a clothing store in the Uttar Pradesh capital.The other accused also have varied educational and professional backgrounds. Arti Soni, 32, from Lucknow, is a Mathematics graduate who worked in corporate event management.A Muttalib, 28, from Kolkata, holds an engineering degree and was engaged in cloth manufacturing and the dairy business.DK Tiwari, 39, an arts graduate, allegedly has business links with Jaiswal, while Jaswant, 29, studied up to Class 12 and worked as an electrician in Lucknow, officials said.The investigation centres on an alleged transnational network that shipped opioid medicines, including Xanax (Alprazolam), Ativan, Tramadol, Valium (Diazepam) and Ambien, from India to customers in the US.The NCB and DEA jointly busted the network in an operation codenamed "Monsoon Thunder".In a statement on November 20, the NCB said records and digital evidence examined so far indicate that the network handled close to 3,000 parcels containing nearly five lakh tablets across the US between June 2022 and November 2026.The agency also shared customer databases covering more than 59,000 subjects with the DEA. These include transaction records, details of past consignments, delivery addresses, USPS tracking IDs and drug types to help identify customers and drop-shippers operating in the US.According to the NCB, Indian operators received drug orders through online platforms such as Telegram, Skype and WhatsApp. The consignments were dispatched through postal and other delivery channels, including the United States Postal Service (USPS).Payments were allegedly routed through digital platforms such as Venmo, bank accounts held in other persons' names, UPI and cryptocurrency, the agency said.
Article Summary: Six Indians arrested in joint India-US investigation into cross-border drug trafficking network. One of the accused, T Manoj, 27, was deported from the US in January 2024 for allegedly trading regulated drugs. Another accused, TD Jaiswal, 30, holds an MBA degree and has business links with a pharmacy and a clothing store in Lucknow.

With Uttarakhand heading towards its next Assembly election, the Pushkar Singh Dhami government has announced a financial assistance scheme for 5.23 lakh rural women, promising Rs 20,000 each under the Baini-Bhuli Yojana. The scheme is set to be launched in December, with the first instalment scheduled to reach beneficiaries’ bank accounts next month.The announcement comes as the ruling BJP government prepares for the electoral contest in the hill state, where women’s welfare, livelihood support and rural development are likely to remain important political issues. He said women’s respect, safety and self-reliance remained among the government’s priorities and that every daughter of Uttarakhand should have equal opportunities for education and progress.State rural development minister Bharat Singh Chaudhary said the scheme would cover women associated with SHGs, the Rural Livelihood Mission and various self-employment activities.Women play a significant role in Uttarakhand’s rural economy through agriculture, animal husbandry, handicrafts and the production of local goods, Chaudhary said. The financial assistance, he added, would support their work and improve livelihood opportunities.The government is also implementing programmes to help women become ‘Lakhpati Didis’, while promoting the branding and marketing of local products and encouraging women entrepreneurs.The Baini-Bhuli Yojana is expected to add to the government’s existing women-focused welfare initiatives as it seeks to highlight its record on economic empowerment ahead of the Assembly election.Asked whether women in urban areas would also be covered, Chaudhary said the government would bring out a separate scheme for them soon.

Article Title: Global South bears brunt of distant wars, India warns UNSC citing Bengal famine
Article Text:
New York, Aug 26 (ANI): India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish (Photo: ANI).

NEW DELHI: India has invoked the devastating Bengal famine of 1943 at the UN Security Council , warning that the economic and humanitarian fallout of global conflicts is borne disproportionately by countries of the Global South.Speaking at a high-level briefing on protecting critical energy infrastructure and Black Sea food supply routes on Monday, India’s permanent representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, said the food, fuel and fertiliser crisis triggered by conflicts was hitting developing nations hardest.“India has consistently emphasised that the costs of conflict are not shared equally,” Parvathaneni said, adding that Global South countries were among those most adversely affected by disruptions caused by wars.Drawing a parallel with World War II, he said the Bengal famine, which killed more than three million people, remained a stark reminder of how people far removed from the battlefield could suffer the consequences of distant conflicts and wartime decisions.“The pain and suffering caused by the devastating Bengal famine of 1943 in India that killed over 3 million people in India, is a stark reminder of the terrible human cost of a distant conflict caused by unchecked wartime priorities and calculations,” he said.The Ukraine conflict, now in its fifth year, has disrupted interconnected supply chains, with consequences extending far beyond the region, Parvathaneni said. Recalling Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for the world to move from “endless war to the end of war”, he said India remained ready to contribute to efforts for a peaceful resolution.India said conflicts deepen food insecurity by disrupting farming, displacing communities, damaging infrastructure and restricting humanitarian access. Their impact spreads through energy and fertiliser supplies, transport networks and agricultural trade, with the Global South bearing a disproportionate burden.“For the Global South, peace is not in the abstract. It is achieved when hungry mouths are fed, when a ship reaches a port, and when a seafarer returns home safe,” Parvathaneni said.India also urged the Security Council to prioritise humanitarian access, protect civilian infrastructure and ensure freedom of navigation, so that humanitarian supplies and legitimate trade could continue without disruption.Parvathaneni said the Black Sea region and India together account for nearly a fifth of global cereal production, while Russia and Ukraine account for almost a quarter of global exports of wheat, maize and barley.He said the importance of the region to global food security showed how disruptions to agricultural production and maritime connectivity could have consequences worldwide.India also highlighted its humanitarian assistance, including wheat supplies to Afghanistan, rice to Sudan and aid to Palestine, as part of its efforts to support global food security.Parvathaneni expressed concern over attacks on merchant vessels and their crews in conflict zones, noting that Indian seafarers had lost their lives in such incidents.“We call for an end to the targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers, and for safe navigation through international waterways to be restored at the earliest,” he said.India and Liberia launched the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers during the UN high-level week in September. Parvathaneni said India was also engaging directly with both sides on shipping safety and grain corridors, while supporting the work of the International Maritime Organisation and the International Labour Organisation.
Article Summary: Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni said the food, fuel and fertiliser crisis triggered by conflicts was hitting developing nations hardest. He said the Bengal famine, which killed more than three million people, remained a stark reminder of how people far removed from the battlefield could suffer the consequences of distant conflicts.

NEW DELHI: Delhi HC has said the Centre's showcause notice and order cancelling the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card of UK-based journalist Amrit Wilson did not specify her anti-India activities. It directed authorities to issue a fresh notice on the grounds.Justice Amit Mahajan passed the order on Wilson's plea challenging Centre's 2023 decision to cancel her OCI card. On Nov 19, HC directed authorities to issue a fresh showcause notice with specific details within a week and allowed Wilson another week to respond. Authorities would then pass an order.It clarified that the existing cancellation order would remain in operation for four weeks or until a fresh order was passed, whichever was earlier.It observed that the lack of specific details had denied Wilson an opportunity to explain her position, and even Centre's reply lacked specific reasons. The court said the notice and order did not detail the alleged anti-India activities, adding that principles of natural justice had not been followed.If the authorities could not spell out specific reasons in the fresh notice, they should provide Wilson with the "gist of the material" while redacting sensitive information or allow her to inspect it, the court said.Centre cancelled Wilson's OCI card in 2023, alleging that she had engaged in "detrimental propaganda against govt". Wilson contended the cancellation order was arbitrary.
Article Summary: Delhi HC said Centre's order cancelling the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card of UK-based journalist Amrit Wilson did not specify her anti-India activities. Article Title: Bisleri controversy puts industry in hot water
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Even as Bisleri on Monday said its mineral water is "safe for consumption, following stringent 90-odd quality checks", the FSSAI action against the popular brand has put the spotlight on compliance and raised the bar across the nearly $4 billion packaged water industry.With Bisleri International accounting for an estimated 60% of the packaged water market, the action may have wider implications across the sector on quality controls, manufacturing processes and labelling practices, industry experts told TOI.The development comes after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) Sunday initiated prosecution against the country's most widely recognised packaged water brand after a sample was found non-compliant with prescribed safety standards.On Monday, the scrutiny seems to have extended beyond Bisleri, with testing and investigations covering other players in the industry. The market led by players such as Bisleri, Coca-Cola's Kinley, PepsiCo's Aquafina and Tata Consumer Products' Himalayan, continues to project a positive long-term growth trajectory, underpinned by population growth, rising per-capita consumption and increasing penetration of branded packaged water across consumer segments.Bisleri could face a short-term impact, but the larger outcome should be a more accountable industry and better consumer protection, notes Lloyd Mathias, independent director, who had stints in senior leadership roles in FMCG and telecom companies. "The tightening of compliance norms is a long overdue move and will ultimately benefit consumers. The packaged water industry has operated with considerable flexibility (on standards), with definitions around purity, mineral content and even the addition of minerals or vitamins often remaining fluid. These need to be clearly and strictly defined, as they are in developed markets, with transparent labelling so consumers know exactly what they are drinking. Companies have also been relatively casual about the labelling (on the pack)," he said.Further, the compliance on the sector has increased over the last two years since it moved under the ambit of FSSAI as a "high-risk food" category in Nov 2024, following the removal of BIS.Typically, enforcement and monitoring in the industry has been weak, allowing even substandard and fake brands to operate. "Greater regulatory oversight is a positive step towards ensuring consistent quality and consumer safety," said an industry expert. Many see it similar to 2003, when CSE's findings on pesticide residue in soft drinks, triggered a wider review of food safety standards and testing.

NEW DELHI: Gaganyaan astronaut-designate and IAF Air Commodore Prasanth B Nair on Monday said that “top industrialists like Ambanis, Adanis and Mahindra should come together to form a space consortium to jointly build advanced space technologies”.“If we have a private space endeavour by the Indian industry, it would be great. India and India Inc., all startups, all organisations in space, including IN-SPACe, ISpA, Isro, IAF and govt need to come together,” said Nair, a Kirti Chakra awardee.Nair, who was a backup pilot for Group Capt Shubhanshu Shukla for the Axiom mission to the International Space Centre, is an experienced fighter and test pilot.On his training along with three other Indian astronaut-designates for the Gaganyaan mission, Air Commodore Nair, whose call sign is ‘Papa’, said, “As we don’t have a ready-made human spaceflight, we are building one; accordingly, our training is an ongoing process and evolving. Procedures of communicating to them, emergency situation system, their escaping from the launchpad in case of an emergency, emergency descent while in orbit and the recovery from ocean after paradropping, all these procedures are actively being done. It is a different level of preparation. We need to build an ecosystem. None of them exists in India, so we are building that. ”On the first unmanned Gaganyaan mission, the astronaut said, “We will learn from the tests on Vyommitra (humanoid) and make necessary adjustments for the manned mission. Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.
