NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Indian-origin billionaire Neil Mehta, wife Jash announce $6 million donation to Trump Accounts for San Francisco children
Article Text:
Neil Mehta and Jash announce $6 million donation to Trump Accounts for San Francisco children.

Who are Neil Mehta and Jash?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Billionaire venture capitalist Neil Mehta and his wife, Jash, announced their contribution of around $6 million to fund $100 to each of the 60,000 children in San Francisco through Trump Accounts. The initiative will give every eligible child born between 2016 and 2024 in the city $100 through the Trump Accounts programme, which allows money to be invested in the stock market and grow over time.“San Francisco has always been a place that believes tomorrow can be better than today,” Neil Mehta said. “It’s why this city has produced so many extraordinary inventions and opportunities. Jash and I want the kids growing up here to feel that same sense of optimism and to own a small piece of the future that it creates.”"The future is going to be wile and wonderful. Own a piece of it," the donor message from the Mehtas read in Trump Accounts.Michae Dell thanked Jash and Neil and called the donation "amazing and wonderful". Michael Dell and Susan Dell committed $6.25 billion to deposit $250 each into the 530A Trump Accounts of 25 million US children.Parents will have to claim and activate their children's accounts through the official government app to receive the contributiosn.The money will remain invested until January 1 of the year the child turns 18. After that, the accounts will be governed by rules similar to those applicable to traditional individual retirement accounts (IRAs), meaning withdrawals could attract taxes or penalties.Children born between 2025 and 2028 are separately eligible for $1,000 in federal seed money under the programme, provided they meet the citizenship and Social Security number requirements. The Mehtas' contribution extends the benefit to an older group of children who do not qualify for that federal seed funding.Neil Mehta is the founder and managing partner of Greenoaks Capital, a prominent investment firm that he co-founded in 2012. He grew up in San Francisco and previously worked at hedge fund DE Shaw before establishing Greenoaks. The investment firm has backed several major technology companies, including Korean e-commerce giant Coupang, cybersecurity company Wiz, artificial intelligence companies Anthropic and Databricks, and financial technology company Stripe.Mehta remained on Coupang's board through its 2021 public listing.Mehta has also become a prominent investor in San Francisco's real estate and community revitalisation efforts. In 2024, he committed $100 million to an initiative aimed at reviving historic buildings and commercial properties along the city's Fillmore Street. He said he had donated his financial interest in the project to a nonprofit. However, the acquisitions attracted criticism from community groups concerned about the displacement of local businesses and the influence of wealthy investors.
Article Summary: Neil Mehta and his wife, Jash, announce $6 million donation to Trump Accounts for San Francisco children. Initiative will give every eligible child born between 2016 and 2024 in the city $100. Michael Dell and Susan Dell committed $6.25 billion to deposit $250 each into the 530A Trump Accounts of 25 million US children.

Article Title: Bengaluru Uber driver shows Rs 4,800 earnings by 10.30pm, claims Rs 20,000 daily income and nearly Rs 6 lakh per month with 10 Ertigas rented out to cabbies in Mumbai, passenger's post goes viral on X
Article Text:
A passenger in Bengaluru learned about a cab driver’s claimed daily earnings which included substantial rental income (AI-generated image used for representative purposes)

‘The numbers look big until you count the expenses’

Drivers, small businesses and income beyond the daily ride





BENGALURU: A routine cab ride to Majestic in Bengaluru turned into an unexpected conversation about money after a passenger asked the driver how much he earned in a day. The answer, however, was not quite what the passenger expected.In a post that has gone viral on X, the passenger said the driver showed him his Uber earnings for the day, which stood at Rs 4,800 at around 10.30pm. The driver reportedly planned to continue working for another two hours.But the bigger surprise came when the conversation shifted from driving to business.According to the viral post, the driver claimed he owned 10 Maruti Suzuki Ertigas in Mumbai, each of which earned him Rs 1,500 in daily rent. That would amount to Rs 15,000 a day from the vehicles, taking his claimed combined daily earnings to around Rs 20,000.The passenger was clearly taken aback by the numbers. Going by the driver's account, an estimated Rs 20,000 a day would add up to nearly Rs 6 lakh a month, if he earns a similar amount every day.The passenger described the amount as remarkable and praised the driver’s hard work, comparing the claimed income with the salary package of a senior manager at a product company.The passenger, in his post, also asked social media users whether they believed the driver’s account or had encountered similar stories.The post triggered conversations about cab ownership, rental income and the earning potential of gig work. Several users shared experiences of drivers who had built businesses beyond their daily rides.One user, while replying under the post, recalled meeting a Bengaluru cab driver who had bought a second vehicle on loan and hired a driver for it, while continuing to drive his first cab himself. The driver, reportedly 35, had also bought land and built a house. His wife worked at a car showroom, and the family took two holidays a year, including flights to Goa. The commenter joked that while the driver flew to Goa, he travelled there by bus.Others, however, urged people not to look at the headline earnings without accounting for expenses. One user wrote, “Interesting conversation. The number looks big till you count the fuel, rent and 12-hour days behind it.”Another one wrote, “A Bangalore cab driver owns 10 Ertigas in Mumbai?”, while one said, “10 Ertigas ~ 2 Crores. FD on this would have brought him Rs 5000 per day, with capital intact.”The post also prompted a user who had recently resigned to joke that the story should be shared on LinkedIn.Another commenter recalled meeting an auto-rickshaw driver whose daughter worked at a leading IT company and who owned three rental apartments in Bengaluru.The discussion also widened to other forms of work.Some users pointed to tea-stall owners and food-delivery workers, arguing that people without conventional degrees or corporate careers could also build substantial incomes through small businesses and gig work.While the cab drivers’ claimed earnings remain unverified, the discussion has highlighted a side of the gig economy that passengers may not always see: for some drivers, the vehicle on the road may be just one part of a larger business.
Article Summary: A passenger in Bengaluru learned about a cab driver’s claimed daily earnings. The driver claimed he owned 10 Maruti Suzuki Ertigas in Mumbai, each of which earned him Rs 1,500 in daily rent. Going by the driver's account, an estimated Rs 20,000 a day would add up to nearly Rs 6 lakh a month.

Article Title: Around 25,000 bank employees to strike on Dec 3 over proposed IDBI Bank sale to Canadian firm Fairfax, likely disrupting 3,700 branches and transactions worth Rs 1,200 crore in Gujarat
Article Text:
IDBI Bank employee unions have called a one-day nationwide strike on December 3

(With Agency Inputs)





AHMEDABAD: Banking operations across Gujarat are likely to be disrupted on December 3 as around 25,000 bank employees and officers are expected to participate in a nationwide strike against the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canadian financial services firm Fairfax Financial Holdings.The strike could affect nearly 3,700 bank branches across Gujarat and disrupt transactions worth around Rs 1,200 crore, according to the Maha Gujarat Bank Employees’ Association (MGBEA).In a strike notice served on IDBI Bank MD and CEO, the UFIOE said the strike would be observed across all branches and offices of the bank nationwide.The All India Bank Employees’ Association (AIBEA), All India Bank Officers’ Association (AIBOA) and Bank Employees Federation of India (BEFI) have called for a solidarity strike in support of IDBI Bank employees and officers.The decision comes despite the government's assurance that the service conditions and pension benefits of existing employees will remain protected after the transaction.The All India Bank Employees' Association (AIBEA), All India Bank Officers Association (AIBOA) and Bank Employees Federation of India (BEFI) have called for a solidarity strike in support of IDBI Bank employees and officers protesting the proposed transfer of control to a foreign investor.The unions termed the proposed sale unwarranted, arguing that public sector banks play a crucial role in safeguarding people's savings. They said IDBI Bank has deposits of around Rs 3.5 lakh crore and advances of Rs 2.5 lakh crore, taking its total business to approximately Rs 6 lakh crore.The December 3 strike comes after IDBI Bank employees and officers staged a two-day protest on November 2 and 3. The unions said the government had continued with the proposed sale despite the earlier agitation.The Union Cabinet approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to a subsidiary of Fairfax Financial Holdings on October 14 for Rs 52,878 crore.As part of the proposed transaction, the government will divest its 30.48 per cent stake in the bank, while the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) will sell its 30.24 per cent holding. Following the transaction, the government's stake will come down to 15 per cent and LIC's shareholding to 19 per cent.However, DIPAM Secretary Arunish Chawla said in October that the share purchase agreement would safeguard the service conditions of existing employees and their pension benefits. He also said a separate pension fund had been set up for existing pensioners and would be fully maintained."Existing employees and existing pensioners should have no apprehensions, as their service conditions have been fully protected," Chawla had said.The proposed disinvestment has also faced criticism from Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, who warned that privatisation could end reservation protections for SC, ST and OBC candidates. He also questioned the move despite IDBI Bank reporting a profit of over Rs 9,000 crore last year.The unions have also flagged concerns over the banking sector's handling of bad loans. They alleged that private corporate borrowers were responsible for large non-performing loans and that banks had incurred losses through loan write-offs.
Article Summary: Around 25,000 bank employees and officers are expected to participate in a nationwide strike. The strike is against the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canadian financial services firm Fairfax Financial Holdings. The decision comes despite the government's assurance that the service conditions and pension benefits of existing employees will remain protected after the transaction.

Article Title: Uttarakhand State Consumer Commission rejects builder's plea to dismiss a house construction complaint, holding that alleged defects and deficiencies in construction fall under consumer law.
Article Text:
The builders filed their written statement on Nov 23, 2021. (AI Image)





DEHRADUN: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held that engaging a builder to construct a house falls within the ambit of the Consumer Protection Act, dismissing a revision petition filed by M/s Sharda Constructions and Developers and its proprietor, Vishw Vijay Singh.The commission found “no illegality or jurisdictional error” in the order passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Dehradun, which had rejected the builders’ application seeking dismissal of a consumer complaint filed by Brij Bhooshan.Bhooshan had filed the complaint on Sept 20, 2021, alleging defects and deficiencies in the construction of his house by the builders. He sought Rs 16.79 lakh, along with 18% annual interest, towards financial losses, Rs 10 lakh for mental agony and another Rs 10 lakh for major construction defects allegedly incapable of being rectified. He also sought litigation costs and other reliefs.The builders filed their written statement on Nov 23, 2021. However, when the matter was listed for their evidence, they moved an application on Feb 17, 2025, under Order 7 Rule 11 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), seeking rejection of the complaint. They contended that the dispute was essentially a money recovery matter and, therefore, fell outside the jurisdiction of the district commission.Challenging the district commission's Sept 16, 2025, order rejecting their application, the builders also referred to proceedings before the Additional District Judge, Commercial Court, Dehradun, arguing that “no cause of action survived”.Opposing the revision petition, the complainant maintained that the dispute concerned deficiency in service and compensation for losses arising from the alleged deficiencies in construction.The commission observed that while deciding an application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the CPC, the averments made in the complaint must be taken into consideration. It held that the complaint clearly pertained to alleged deficiency in service and that whether such deficiency existed would be determined on the merits of the case.In its Nov 19 order, the state commission also noted that the builders had moved the application nearly two years after the matter had been fixed for their evidence, suggesting that the move was intended to delay the disposal of the complaint. Dismissing the revision petition, it directed both parties to appear before the district commission on Nov 30.
Article Summary: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held that engaging a builder to construct a house falls within the ambit of the Consumer Protection Act. M/s Sharda Constructions and Developers and its proprietor, Vishw Vijay Singh, had filed a revision petition. Brij Bhooshan had filed the complaint on Sept 20, 2021.

Article Title: Bengaluru man gets Rs 4 ‘location surcharge’ on medicines, fights MedPlus in consumer court, pharmacy ordered to pay Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 2,000 costs
Article Text:
(AI IMAGE) A 36-year-old resident of Sarjapura challenged a Rs 4 surcharge levied by the pharmacy chain MedPlus





BENGALURU: It was only Rs 4, but a 36-year-old Sarjapura resident refused to let it go. Charged a "location surcharge" on top of the printed price of his medicines, he fought it for months, first by email and then in the consumer court. The Bangalore (Urban) District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has now held pharmacy chain MedPlus guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The dispute began on September 25, 2025, when the complainant bought medicines from the MedPlus Pharmacy outlet in Sarjapura for Rs 1,113. The invoice carried an extra line, "Location Surcharge Fees", of Rs 4, inclusive of GST, even though medicines are sold at the maximum retail price (MRP).He emailed the company the same day and sent follow-ups and reminders until October 3, asking for a refund and for the practice to stop. The company's reply, the commission noted, was that "ongoing maintenance costs" across its locations had forced it to introduce a small surcharge to help maintain its shops. He received no refund, only a reply citing maintenance costs.On January 19, 2026, he approached the commission, appearing in person.He sought a refund of Rs 4, Rs 1 lakh for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 10,000 for litigation and incidental costs. Optival Health Solutions Pvt. Ltd., which operates MedPlus, and its Sarjapura branch did not appear despite notice, nor did they file a reply. The commission placed them ex parte.Relying on a National Commission ruling, Kotak Mahindra Old Mutual vs Dr Nishi Gupta, the commission held that not filing a written version amounts to admission of the complaint's allegations. It added that the company's own email replies admitted the surcharge was being collected, and that the invoice showed it plainly.The commission rejected the maintenance argument. It said the MRP already covers taxes, retailer margin, transport and maintenance, and that shop upkeep is a business overhead to be met from the retailer's profit margin. It cannot be passed on to customers as a fee without prior disclosure and consent. It noted that charging above MRP is an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and that the Legal Metrology rules and the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, bar the sale of medicines above the printed MRP. Consumer fora, it said, have consistently held that no retailer can charge even a rupee over MRP under labels such as handling or convenience fees.The commission, comprising president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani, on October 30 allowed the complaint in part. It directed both companies, jointly and severally, to pay the Rs 4 surcharge, Rs 5,000 as compensation for deficiency in service and Rs 2,000 towards litigation costs, within 45 days
Article Summary: A 36-year-old resident of Sarjapura challenged a Rs 4 surcharge levied by the pharmacy chain MedPlus. The Bangalore (Urban) District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has now held MedPlus guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.

Article Title: ICICI life insurance rejects Rs 1.75 lakh insurance claim citing pre-existing hypertension; Varanasi consumer commission directs bank to pay Rs 2 lakh within 30 days
Article Text:
ICICI life insurance





LUCKNOW: The Varanasi District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission on November 11 directed ICICI life insurance to pay an insurance claim of Rs 2 lakh to a complainant within 30 days.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (Consumer Forum) issued the order following a complaint filed by Dhirendranath Sharma, who met with an accident on April 20, 2025, while riding a motorcycle.Sharma sustained a severe head injury in the accident. He had to undergo surgery at a hospital in Lucknow after his condition failed to improve despite treatment at several hospitals.The treatment also cost him a substantial amount.According to the complainant, he had secured an insurance policy with ICICI life insurance for a sum of Rs 15 lakh and had been paying the premiums regularly.However, when he filed a claim of Rs 1.75 lakh to cover his medical expenses, the bank rejected it, citing that he had been suffering from hypertension for 10 years and was on regular medication for high blood pressure.The complainant then approached the Varanasi consumer forum seeking relief. The forum ruled in his favour.
Article Summary: ICICI life insurance to pay an insurance claim of Rs 2 lakh to a complainant within 30 days. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission issued the order following a complaint filed by Dhirendranath Sharma. Sharma met with an accident on April 20, 2025, while riding a motorcycle.

Article Title: India's ageing Barak missile shield gets Rs 1,976 crore upgrade: What changes
Article Text:
A Barak-1 missile being fired from an Israeli warship during a live fire drill. (Image credit: Israeli armed forces)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The defence ministry has signed a Rs 1,976.40 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries for the upgradation and obsolescence management of the Barak point defence missile system fitted on Indian warships. Under the deal, IAI will carry out a comprehensive overhaul of the system's hardware and software, which the ministry says will give naval platforms enhanced features and a potent anti-air defence capability.The announcement stresses capability, but obsolescence management is arguably the heart of the contract. The Barak-1 entered service around 2000 and has been deployed for over two decades on Delhi-class destroyers, Shivalik-class and Brahmaputra-class frigates and the aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya. Many of its electronic components, processors and sensors are now ageing, and in several cases the original manufacturers no longer produce spares, making readiness increasingly expensive to sustain.Two practical considerations explain the need for modernisation of the point defence system. Replacing every installation would cost far more and disrupt operations more than upgrading systems already integrated into the fleet, and many of these ships will serve for years. DRDO 's indigenous VL-SRSAM is meant to succeed the Barak-1, but fleet-wide induction will take time.The upgrade ensures no capability gap in the interim. Better software, computing power and fire-control can improve reaction time, reliability, availability and resistance to jamming, even if the missile itself remains the same.The deal also underlines why point-defence systems matter. They form the last layer of an integrated air-defence network, protecting specific assets such as ships, airbases, radars and command centres against threats that slip past outer defences. On a warship, the Barak-1 is that final missile layer against aircraft, drones and anti-ship missiles. Warships are also equipped with gun based close in weapon systems such as the AK-630 which form the final line of defence.Cheap drones, loitering munitions and faster, low-flying missiles shorten reaction time, while the Russia-Ukraine conflict has shown how massed drones can be used against airbases and logistics hubs.Using costly long-range interceptors against inexpensive drones is an unfavourable trade, so shorter-range systems help conserve missiles for graver threats. The danger is saturation, where a defender runs out of interceptors even after intercepting everything.For India, with airbases and forward positions spread along the northern and western borders, layered cover is essential. DRDO's VSHORADS cleared three flight trials on February 27 this year, and the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System, combining QRSAM, VSHORADS and a laser-based weapon, had its maiden trials on August 23, 2025. The Defence Acquisition Council cleared VSHORADS and medium-range missile procurement for the Army on July 3.The Barak contract is thus less a missile purchase than a sustainment effort. It also reinforces the India-Israel defence partnership, which includes the jointly developed Barak-8.
Article Summary: India has signed a Rs 1,976.40 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries. IAI will carry out a comprehensive overhaul of the system's hardware and software. The Barak-1 entered service around 2000 and has been deployed for over two decades.

Article Title: Shiv Nadar tops philanthropy list for fifth year; India's richest donate Rs 11,554 crore
Article Text:
Shiv Nadar and his family retained their position as India's top philanthropists, donating Rs 2,593 crore.





MUMBAI: HCL founder Shiv Nadar and his family have retained the title of India's most generous philanthropists for the fifth consecutive year, donating Rs 2,593 crore in 2025-26, or an average of Rs 7.1 crore every day, according to the EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List 2026 released on Friday.The report, now in its 13th edition, shows that 219 philanthropists collectively donated Rs 11,554 crore during the financial year, an increase of 11% over the Rs 10,380 crore recorded last year. The number of philanthropists on the list has risen from 192 to 219, while new entrants have nearly quadrupled from 12 to 45.Gautam Adani and his family climbed three places to the second position after more than doubling their contribution to Rs 877 crore, an increase of 127%. The Bajaj family retained third place with Rs 632 crore, followed by Mukesh Ambani and family at Rs 620 crore.Nandan Nilekani ranked fifth with Rs 380 crore, followed by Kumar Mangalam Birla and family (Rs 366 crore), Cyrus and Adar Poonawalla (Rs 336 crore), Sudhir and Samir Mehta (Rs 334 crore), Ranjan Pai and family (Rs 219 crore) and Rohini Nilekani (Rs 215 crore).Education continued to attract the largest share of philanthropic contributions, receiving Rs 4,188 crore, accounting for 36% of the total donations.As many as 200 of the 219 philanthropists supported education, while it was the primary cause for 95 donors.Healthcare emerged as another major beneficiary, with donations rising 82% to Rs 1,768 crore. Contributions towards arts, culture and heritage stood at Rs 1,377 crore, while environment and sustainability attracted Rs 813 crore, an increase of 86%.Rohini Nilekani emerged as India's most generous woman philanthropist with a contribution of Rs 215 crore, followed by Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw (Rs 93 crore) and Anu Aga and family (Rs 78 crore), Bina Shah of Harish and Bina Shah Foundation (Rs 77.5 crore). The number of women philanthropists increased from 24 to 29.Mumbai continued to lead the country in the number of philanthropists, with 64 individuals, seven more than last year. New Delhi followed with 41 and Bengaluru with 20. However, New Delhi topped the list in terms of donation value at Rs 3,168 crore, marginally ahead of Mumbai's Rs 3,007 crore.The report also highlighted the growing participation of self-made entrepreneurs. Of the 219 philanthropists, 125 were self-made, accounting for 57% of the list and 65% of the total donations.Among the new entrants were Motilal Oswal Financial Services co-founders Raamdeo Agrawal and Motilal Oswal, who contributed Rs 120 crore and Rs 119 crore respectively. New York-based Chandrika and Ranjan Tandon donated Rs 100 crore towards establishing a School of Artificial Intelligence at IIM Ahmedabad.Last year, India overtook China with more donors giving Rs 100 crore or more, this year, China has 30 donors versus 19 Indians who donated more than Rs 100 crore.Despite the growing number of donors, philanthropic contributions remained concentrated among a relatively small group. The top 10 philanthropists accounted for Rs 6,572 crore, or 57% of all donations, while just 19 individuals who donated Rs 100 crore or more contributed 68% of the total.Naghma Mulla, CEO of EdelGive Foundation, said the growing number of new entrants reflected a shift in how wealthy Indians viewed philanthropy. "In 2014, a year after we started publishing the list, we had 50 philanthropists on it. This year, we have 219. That is a 338% increase," she said.Anas Rahman Junaid, founder and chief researcher of Hurun India, said India's growing wealth was opening a new chapter in philanthropy, with entrepreneurs increasingly choosing to give back while continuing to build their businesses.The report, however, also flagged a concern in corporate social responsibility spending. While CSR expenditure by BSE 200 companies stood at Rs 18,922 crore, unspent CSR funds rose to a record Rs 2,290 crore, resulting in the widest net shortfall in more than a decade.
Article Summary: The EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List 2026 was released on Friday. The report, now in its 13th edition, shows that 219 philanthropists collectively donated Rs 11,554 crore during the financial year. Education continued to attract the largest share of philanthropic contributions.

Article Title: Bombay HC directs internal audit of Kanjurmarg waste facility; seeks citizen participation is waste segregation
Article Text:
The HC appreciate the proactive steps taken by the Municipal Corporation, especially its appeal to citizens to segregate wet and dry waste and a compliance mechanism for residential bulk waste generators

The issues HC flagged

MUMBAI: Observing that an internal audit of the dumping facility at Kanjurmarg was lacking, the Bombay high court has directed a monitoring committee to undertake one to assess how its functioning can be improved and to suggest immediate improvements to effectively address citizens’ grievances of odour, public health risks and what it said was the biggest challenge to ecology—plastics.Appreciating BMC's appeal to segregate wet and dry waste, HC division bench of Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said, "If citizens adopt an appropriate approach...it would go a long way towards addressing the urgent problems faced by citizens at large.''With over 7,000 metric tonnes of daily waste available, it is imperative to convert it for beneficial use including power generation, HC said in a November 18 order, out on Friday night.The HC addressed ongoing pollution and odour issues at BMC’s Kanjurmarg waste management facility calling for technological improvements, waste segregation at source, and development of a comprehensive policy for slum areas. The order, which included photos from a recent site visit by the Judges, emphasized the need for effective waste management, plastic ban enforcement, and AI enabled technological solutions to reduce environmental harm and protect public health.Authorities must urgently implement and pilot systematic segregation of wet and dry waste at the point of generation—especially in challenging wards—to reduce operational burdens and facilitate effective processing, the HC said and directed the committee and municipal corporation to consider advanced waste management technologies, such as converting waste to energy and possibly employing incineration, and to evaluate a potential ban on single-use plastics.The HC order seeking to establish lasting improvements for the city’s waste management framework, also directed the State to form a high-level committee to scientifically address garbage management in slum areas, which generate about 50% of Mumbai’s total waste, and to frame new norms for enforcing civic discipline in these zones.The HC order came in petitions filed by Kannamwar Co-op Housing Society Association and Sanjay Yelve highlighting health concerns due to the site’s proximity. On November 3, the HC had flagged “two fundamental issues” of the odour and lack of segregation wet and dry waste at the Kanjurmarg site.The HC said it appreciated innovative steps taken by the BrihanMumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) to improve public health, hygiene and cleanliness and installation of AI enabled CCTV cameras but added “However, what disturbed us was that the operations at the Kanjurmarg facility continued to generate odour and pollution, which had been the subject matter of persistent complaints of the large population residing in the areas surrounding the Kanjurmarg facility. ”“These areas include Vikhroli, Bhandup, Mulund, etc. and the lakhs of residents being adversely affected by such menace,’’ the HC said.The waste includes regular domestic household waste and that from municipal markets, like meat, vegetable markets apart from tonnes of plastic articles of every kind, cloth, cans, bottles, household sanitary waste, etc. are also received at the site said the HC. “The herculean efforts involved in segregation activity being undertaken at the site are beyond dispute,’’ the HC observed after hearing counsel Abhijit Rane for residents, amicus curiage senior counsel Sharan Jagtiani, senior counsel Anil Sakhare for BMC, Jaya Bagwe for MPCB, Saket Mone for the facility operator and AGP Jyoti Chavan for State but said the “major source of odour is the process of segregating and removing dry waste from the wet waste. ’’The HC posted the matter to December 7 for further hearing including the internal audit to be undertaken by the monitoring committee.· Need for Waste Segregation at Source: Lack of segregation of wet and dry waste at the collection source is a major factor causing operational challenges and odour at the facility. The court emphasized that effective waste segregation at source would resolve many issues and improve waste processing efficiency.· Large Contribution from Slum Areas: Slum areas account for around 50% of Mumbai’s total garbage generation. The court found current legal provisions inadequate to ensure proper health and hygiene in these zones and recommended formulating robust policies and norms for slum waste management.· Proactive Steps and Public Sensitization: Initiatives such as installing AI-enabled CCTVs and publishing public appeals for responsible waste management were recognized. However, the court stressed the need to intensify citizen sensitization about not dumping garbage on streets and the importance of adopting systematic waste segregation practices.· Exploration of Advanced Solutions: The court recommended considering technological advancements (like incineration for power generation), evaluating a complete ban on single-use plastic bags, conducting an internal audit of the facility, collecting health data from medical practitioners in affected areas, and launching pilot projects for waste segregation in challenging city areas.Citizen Sensitization and Public Initiatives: Municipal authorities are instructed to intensify public awareness efforts about proper waste disposal, including screening educational films, running social media campaigns, and publishing advertisements. Compliance with segregation and management rules is set as mandatory, with penalties for violations.
Article Summary: The Bombay high court has directed a monitoring committee to undertake one to assess how its functioning can be improved. The HC addressed ongoing pollution and odour issues at BMC’s Kanjurmarg waste management facility. The order, which included photos from a recent site visit, emphasized the need for effective waste management, plastic ban enforcement, and AI enabled technological solutions.

The offering comprised 980 million shares priced at $83 apiece, making it the largest IPO on record and one of the biggest public listings in the technology sector.The company's shares opened at $111.50, a premium of 34.34% over the IPO price, and climbed to an intraday high of $115.10 before paring gains. Article Title: Gurgaon couple buys sandals for Rs 2,429, heel bends on first use, showroom refuses replacement and offers repairs, consumer commission orders full refund with 9% interest and Rs 26,000 compensation a
Article Text:
(AI IMAGE) Deepak Gupta and his wife Shweta faced a not-so-great experience with defective sandals right after they bought them





GURGAON: A pair of sandals bought for Rs 2,429 developed a defect on its first use, but when the buyers approached the showroom, they were offered repairs instead of a replacement. Rejecting the footwear company’s repair-only warranty policy, the Gurgaon consumer commission has ordered it to refund the purchase price and pay Rs 26,000 in compensation and litigation costs.Deepak Gupta and his wife Shweta bought the sandals from Stelatoes Shoes & Accessories Pvt Ltd’s Gurudwara Road showroom on Aug 30, 2025. The salesperson allegedly assured them that the footwear was a fresh piece and carried a six-month replacement warranty in case of any defect.However, when Shweta wore the sandals for the first time on Sept 1, the heel bent and the adhesive came loose, the couple alleged. They returned to the showroom on Sept 3, but the manager allegedly blamed the damage on her twisting her foot and refused to replace the footwear, offering only repairs.After their repeated requests for a refund went unanswered, the couple approached the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.Advocate Chandan Yadav, representing the complainants, relied on their affidavit, purchase invoice and photographs of the sandals. The company’s authorised representative, Akshay Sharma, argued that the terms printed on the invoice excluded refunds and allowed only repairs within the 90-day warranty period. He said the company was willing to repair the footwear.The commission, headed by president Sanjeev Jindal with members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur, rejected the defence, observing that a company could not benefit from its own wrongdoing after selling poor-quality goods. It held that unilateral warranty conditions placing consumers at a disadvantage could not override their rights.The panel also noted that the company failed to produce any evidence to rebut the complainants’ allegations. Holding that the company had committed deficiency in service and adopted an unfair trade practice, it allowed the complaint.The opposite parties were directed to refund Rs 2,428.99 with 9% annual interest from Aug 30, 2025, and pay Rs 15,000 for mental harassment and Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses.

The salesperson allegedly assured them that the footwear was a fresh piece and carried a six- month replacement warranty in case of any defect. The heel bent and the adhesive came loose, the couple alleged. The manager allegedly blamed the damage on her twisting her foot and offered only repairs.

Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, breaks below 94 against dollar: What's next
Article Text:
Rupee moves below 94 against US dollar

Crude oil prices cool as hopes of peace grow

Foreign fund inflows add to rupee's support

NEW DELHI: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East.The currency rose 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade. It opened at around 93.85 in the interbank forex market before gaining further. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98 against the greenback.Forex traders said rupee could maintain its positive momentum if diplomatic efforts in the Middle East make progress. Any easing of tensions could reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices, providing further support to the currency.These hopes gained ground over the weekend after US President Donald Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement.The easing in crude oil prices has been one of the key factors supporting rupee. Brent crude, which had earlier climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. Amit Pabari, managing director of CR Forex Advisors, said improving diplomatic expectations were already having an impact on energy prices."The improvement in diplomatic expectations is already reflecting in energy prices. Brent crude, which had climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. For currency markets, even the possibility of a lasting agreement is important," Pabari said.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.15% lower at $98.17 per barrel in futures trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was also down 0.12% at 102.18.Foreign investment activity provided another source of support for the domestic currency. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.The combination of lower crude prices and stronger foreign fund inflows has supported the rupee's recent gains against the dollar.With rupee now below the 94-per-dollar level, Pabari sees further room for appreciation. He expects the currency to move towards 93.50 and 93.00, while identifying 94.40–94.50 as the immediate resistance zone."With USD/INR breaking below the 94.00 mark, the probability of further rupee appreciation towards 93.50 and 93.00 has increased. On the upside, 94.40–94.50 is likely to act as the immediate resistance zone," Pabari said.Meanwhile, domestic equity markets opened lower on Monday. BSE Sensex fell 93.95 points to 80,919.19, while NSE Nifty declined 30 points to 24,968.80.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30.
Article Summary: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98.
